claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you check your eligibility for Child Benefit! Let me start by getting the first step of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! I can see the assessment has started. To help you, I need to ask you about your child or children.

**First, let me ask: How old is your child (or what are the ages of your children)?**

This is important because eligibility rules vary depending on whether they are:
- **Under 16** years old
- **16 to 19** years old (may qualify if in education or training)
- **20 years old or over** (generally not eligible)

Please tell me about all the children you'd like me to check eligibility for, including their names and ages.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who's 17 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, **Alex, who is 17 years old**. This means Alex falls into the 16-19 age category.

For young people aged 16-19, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether they're in education or training. Let me ask you the next question:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or an approved training course?**

This includes things like:
- Secondary school or college
- University or higher education
- Approved apprenticeships or training schemes
- Other approved education/training programmes

Please let me know Alex's current status.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. They finished school but haven't gone on to college or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So Alex is 17 years old and is **not currently in education or training**.

Since Alex is in the 16-19 age group but not in education or training, I need to check whether there might be any extension to eligibility. Let me navigate to the next step to see what other factors might apply.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news - there's a potential extension. Even though Alex isn't currently in education or training, if they **left education recently**, there may still be eligibility for a limited period.

**The question is: When did Alex finish school or leave education?**

Specifically, did Alex leave education/training within the last **20 weeks**? (That's roughly 5 months from when they left.)

This is important because there's a grace period after leaving education where you may still be eligible for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex left school over a year ago now, so it's been well past 20 weeks.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex left school over a year ago (well beyond the 20-week extension period) and is not currently in education or training, I'm afraid this means Alex no longer qualifies as a qualifying child for Child Benefit purposes.

Let me navigate to confirm the outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Here's why:**

Child Benefit eligibility for young people aged 16-19 requires that they be in approved education or training. While there is a 20-week grace period after leaving education (during which you can still claim if they register with the careers service or armed services), Alex left school over a year ago, which is well beyond this extension period.

**The rules are:**
- Children under 16: automatically qualify
- Ages 16-19: must be in approved education/training to qualify
- 20+: not eligible
- Extension: If a 16-17 year old leaves education, there's a 20-week period during which they can still qualify if they register with careers service or armed services

**What you might want to consider:**
- If Alex does enter approved education or training in the future, you could potentially claim from that point onwards
- You may wish to contact HMRC directly if you have any questions about this decision

I'm sorry I couldn't deliver better news. Is there anything else I can help clarify about Child Benefit eligibility?
